opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, clubs, warehouses and head office.

follow100Note: The stores earned $4.24 of operating profit from every $100 of revenue; a $794M investment gain, tax and partners' shares left $3.16. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $5,104M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $5,307M, of which $203M belongs to noncontrolling interests.

kpis.label: U.S. comp sales
kpis.note: excludes fuel; transactions and ticket both up

oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was a $794M gain this quarter versus a $2,995M loss a year ago — unrealized fair-value moves on equity investments Walmart holds. Adjusted EPS of $0.60 excludes the net-of-tax effect of the investment gain ($0.05 per share) and business reorganization charges ($0.02 per share).
otherDetail: Interest of $600M, net, offset by a $794M gain on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: Stores and eCommerce in the United States — comparable sales rose 3.8% and segment operating income rose 7.0%.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and eCommerce outside the U.S. — net sales rose 12.1% and segment operating income jumped 31.7%.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: Walmart's warehouse clubs in the United States — comparable sales rose 3.5% excluding fuel.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Membership fees from Sam's Club and Walmart+, plus other income — small, but nearly cost-free.

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 9.6% to $6,841M on 6.0% revenue growth — the gross margin rate widened 42 basis points, membership income grew 21%, and global eCommerce sales rose 21%, led by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery and the marketplace.
takeaways.title: Operating income outgrew sales

takeaways.text: Below the operating line, Walmart booked a $794M gain on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves on stakes it holds. A year ago the same line was a $2,995M loss; that swing is the main reason headline profit tripled to $5,104M.
takeaways.title: A paper gain, not just store gains

takeaways.text: The global advertising business grew 24%, including 26% for Walmart Connect in the U.S. — high-margin revenue that sits on top of the store business. Global inventory fell 2.7%, with U.S. inventory down 4.2%.
takeaways.title: Ads are becoming a real business

verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 6.0% to $161.5B and operating income grew 9.6% as U.S. comparable sales rose 3.8% and eCommerce jumped 21% — and a $794M paper gain on its investment stakes helped lift headline profit to $5.1B, from $1.7B a year ago.
